chunks: There has come to me from you a connected advice, and an embellished letter, which you have written due to your misguidance, and despatched due to your poor judgment,
This is the letter of a man who has neither insight to guide him, nor a leader to direct him,
Passion called him and he responded to it, and misguidance led him and he followed it,
Consequently, he began to speak nonsense, and went astray recklessly.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the spiritual and intellectual state of Muawiya in his letter?
ai.summary: In this epistle to Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the Umayyad governor’s letter as a manifestation of *hawa* (capricious desire) and *dalal* (misguidance), contrasting it with the clarity of the Ahl al-Bayt. He characterizes Muawiya as lacking *basar* (spiritual insight) and a *qaid* (guiding leader), thereby highlighting the Shia theological distinction between political authority derived from divine guidance and that derived from worldly ambition. This passage underscores the concept of *ghaww* (deviation) where one follows their lower self rather than the Imam, a key theme in Nahj al-Balagha's political theology.
